subject: Data Engineering
title: ACID Transactions on Lakes
description: Learn ACID Transactions on Lakes in one minute.

hook.text: Two Spark jobs update the same table simultaneously. With ACID, both succeed safely. Without it, data corruption.

buildup.text: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability — the guarantees every database provides.

discovery.text: Table formats bring ACID to files by writing new files and atomically updating a metadata pointer.

twist.text: Writes never modify existing files. They create new ones and swap the metadata. The old files remain for time travel.

climax.text: ACID on lakes means you can run concurrent jobs, handle failures, and guarantee consistent reads.

punchline.text: New files, atomic swaps. That's ACID for the lake.

quiz.question: How do table formats achieve ACID transactions on object storage?
options: By writing new files and atomically updating metadata pointers
By locking the entire bucket during writes
By using a traditional relational database underneath
